name: SIRTOM — Factorial HR software rollout
description: Internship at a public waste authority: I rolled out the Factorial HR software for all 73 staff, replacing paper and Excel, and got everyone on board, including field teams with little or no digital literacy.
context: SIRTOM de la région Flers-Condé runs household waste collection around Flers-Condé, in Normandy. I interned at its head office from 13 May to 12 August 2024.

HR ran on paper, with an Excel absence file. The authority had Factorial, a cloud HR software, but nobody knew how to use it. My job: take it over, fit it to the authority's rules and get every department using it. It was live three weeks before I left, which gave me time to follow adoption and help on other projects.

Today the authority uses it for time tracking or schedules for around a hundred staff, leave and absences, a simpler approval path, personal and shared documents, and staff information (for example the professional elections of 10 December 2026).

work.title: Taking over the software
work.text: Self-taught, well enough that the general director wrote in her recommendation letter that I knew it better than the vendor.

work.title: Full HR configuration
work.text: Every paper or Excel process moved in, set to the authority's own rules.
points: Time tracking (clock-in), schedules and payroll.
Employment statuses: public-sector contract staff, fixed-term, permanent and more.
Leave balances: paid leave, RTT days, recoverable hours, counter resets, carry-over between years.
Organisation chart, approvals and permissions: each manager sees and approves only their team.
HR documents in one place.

work.title: Fitting real constraints
points: Many statuses, each with its own leave and hour rules.

Collection crews work one week on, one week off, a rotation Factorial doesn't support. My workaround: two schedules per employee with alternating validity periods, entered up to their likely retirement age. I left a wide margin rather than ask anyone their age. It now runs on its own.

work.title: Training and adoption
points: No time for one-to-one training, so documentation per department, each team getting only its part.
Some crew members had very limited computer skills and some struggled to read, so I made visual and video tutorials instead: watch, then repeat.
After go-live: lots of questions answered, people trained, the most reluctant won over.

work.title: Results
points: Several hours of HR work saved every week.
Fewer lost documents, records far easier to find.
More accurate time tracking than paper, which was easy to get wrong or misuse.

note: No screenshots: dashboards and documentation hold employees' personal data and internal processes.

name: ChauffeChauffe — CRM & ERP prototype
description: Team school project: a clickable CRM/ERP prototype for a heating repair company, built when the assignment only asked for a feature plan and mock-ups.
context: ChauffeChauffe is a fictional family business repairing water heaters in Poitiers, used as a class case: a complaint from a client left without heating for over a month, statements from the secretary and technicians, and their paper call slip.
Our team went beyond the requested plan and built a prototype anyone can click through. A team effort, not mine alone.

work.title: Diagnosis
work.text: Why the client waited a month:
points: A paper planner, with technicians booking clients without telling the secretary.
Parts ordered only after the landlord posted back a signed invoice, left untouched two days on delivery, a second part forgotten.
No shared knowledge: manuals and notes kept in personal folders, annotated paper or memory, so the next technician arrived without the history.

work.title: What the prototype covers
points: Client files (address, equipment model, maintenance contract) and a weekly team calendar showing real constraints (finishes at 3:30 pm, new hire, prefers distant jobs…), so the secretary plans with them, not around them.
A parts pipeline from approval to delivery, with an estimated date on each order.
A shared knowledge base per equipment model: manuals, procedures, safety notes and field tips, open to new hires.
Billing from draft to payment (draft, sent, paid, cancelled), totals invoiced, collected and pending, the tenant/owner cost split that blocked the repair, CSV export.

work.title: What it is
work.text: A clickable front end on local demo data inspired by the case: the experience and data model, with no real back end.
